items.headline: Spotify Opens AI Audiobook Creation Tools to All US Indie Authors; Webtoon Launches AI Translation
items.excerpt: Spotify has taken its ElevenLabs-powered Audiobook Creation Tools out of beta and opened AI narration to every US indie author inside Spotify for Authors. The same roundup covers Webtoon's new opt-in AI translation for self-published creators — two production steps that used to cost authors thousands now sitting behind a dashboard button.

items.headline: Large Scale Digitization in the AI Era: Model Terms for Libraries and Their AI Partners
items.excerpt: The Center for Research Libraries has published an issue paper giving libraries concrete contract language for the wave of proposals to digitize their collections at scale for commercial AI training. It covers ownership, permitted uses, public access, compensation and attribution — a negotiating template for anyone whose stacks are being courted as a dataset.

items.headline: Folk Taxonomy: The Insecurity Behind the Em-Dash Panic
items.excerpt: Editors and agents are increasingly 'detecting' AI prose by surface tells — the Aptos font, the em dash, the 'it's not this, it's that' construction — without reading the work. TNPS argues this folk taxonomy is punishing human writers for ordinary style choices and substituting superstition for literary judgement.

items.headline: Reimagining Research Papers as Interactive and Reliable AI Agents
items.excerpt: A new Nature paper introduces Paper2Agent, a framework that converts a published research paper into a working AI agent, turning the article from a passive artefact into something a reader can query and run. For scholarly publishers and librarians it reframes what a 'paper' is as a publishing format.
